title: The jury in a civil trial
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers juries deciding guilt in criminal trials, but the new point is about six jurors deciding facts, liability and damages in civil trials, which is a different idea.

draft.title: The jury in a civil trial
card: A civil trial may be heard with a jury. A civil jury has six people, and not every civil trial has one.
The jury decides the facts. It weighs the evidence and decides what happened.
The jury also decides whether the defendant is liable, which means legally responsible for the harm.
In some cases the jury also decides the damages, the amount of money awarded to the plaintiff. The judge manages the trial and explains the law.
draft.remember: A civil jury of six decides the facts and liability, and sometimes the damages.

a.q: How many people make up a jury in a civil trial?
a.why: A civil jury has six people. Twelve is tempting because it is the usual number in a criminal trial, but it is not the number in a civil trial.
a.clue: It is fewer than in a criminal jury.

b.q: In a civil trial with a jury, who decides whether the defendant is liable?
b.why: The jury decides the facts and whether the defendant is liable. The judge is tempting, but the judge manages the trial and explains the law, while the jury makes the decision on liability.
b.clue: Who decides the facts in a jury trial?

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly says a Victorian civil jury has six people and decides the facts, liability and sometimes damages, and both questions have one clear right answer.
